training.sudoku_full_house: When a row, column or box has one empty square left, the digit it's missing goes there.
training.sudoku_hidden_single_box: Pick a box and a digit it still needs. When every other empty square in the box already sees that digit in its row or column, the one square left must hold it.
training.sudoku_hidden_single_line: The same idea along a row or column: when every other empty square in the line already sees a digit in its column, row or box, the one square left takes it.
training.sudoku_naked_single: Look at one square instead of one digit. When its row, column and box between them hold eight different digits, the ninth is the only one left for it.
training.sudoku_locked: When a digit's places in a box all lie in one row or column, it must go there, so the rest of that line can't have it. (The same works the other way round, a line's places all in one box.) That often leaves a single.
training.sudoku_naked_pair: Two squares in a row, column or box that can each be only the same two digits take both of them, so no other square there can hold either. Strike them off and look for the single it leaves.
training.sudoku_hidden_pair: Two digits that fit in only the same two squares of a row, column or box take those squares, so those two squares can't hold anything else. Look for the single that follows.
training.sudoku_what_if: A square with two digits left, or a digit with two places left: suppose one and follow it a step or two. If something runs out of digits or places, the other choice is the answer.
training.cage_full_house: When a row, column or box has one empty square left, the digit it's missing goes there.
training.cage_cage_last: When a cage has one empty square left, it takes whatever the cage's total still needs.
training.cage_hidden_single_box: Pick a box and a digit it still needs. When every other empty square in the box already sees that digit, or its cage already has one, the one square left must hold it.
training.cage_hidden_single_line: The same idea along a row or column: when every other empty square in the line already sees a digit, the one square left takes it.
training.cage_naked_single: Look at one square. When its row, column, box and cage between them hold eight different digits, the ninth is the only one left for it.
training.cage_cage_combo: A cage's total can only be made a few ways with digits that don't repeat. A 3 in two squares is 1 and 2; a 17 is 8 and 9. List the ways that still fit and see what they leave.
training.cage_forty_five: Every row, column and box adds up to 45. Add the cages lying wholly inside one and take that from 45: the squares left over must make the difference.
training.cage_linked_totals: Two or three totals that share squares: settle one, and it cuts the others. Work them through one after another until a square has one digit left.
training.cage_cage_chain: A longer line of totals: each cage or 45-rule group strikes digits from its squares, which narrows the next. Some lines come back to a total twice, or close in on a digit's places from two sides. Follow them until a square has one digit left.
training.inequality_last: When a row or column has one empty square left, the digit it's missing goes there.
training.inequality_only_digit: Look at one square. When its row and column between them hold every digit but one, that one is all it can be.
training.inequality_only_place: Pick a line and a digit it still needs. When every other empty square in it already has that digit in its own row or column, the one square left takes it.
training.inequality_sign_bound: A sign points at the smaller side. A square smaller than another can't be the biggest digit, and one bigger can't be 1; along a chain of signs the bounds add up. Count them in and see what's left for the square.
training.inequality_sign_place: The same as a digit's only place in a line, with the signs counted too: a square the signs keep below a digit can't hold it.
training.inequality_naked_pair: Two squares in a line that can each be only the same two digits take both of them, so no other square in that line can hold either. Strike them off and look for the single it leaves.
training.inequality_hidden_pair: Two digits that fit in only the same two squares of a line take those squares, so those two squares can't hold anything else. Look for the single that follows.
training.regions_last: When a region has one empty square left, the digit it's missing goes there.
training.regions_only_digit: Look at one square. Its region's digits and the digits touching it, even at a corner, rule digits out. When only one is left, that's it.
training.regions_only_place: Pick a region and a digit it still needs. When every other empty square in it touches that digit already, the one square left takes it.
training.regions_locked: When every place a region's digit could go touches the same square outside the region, that square can't be that digit. That often leaves a single.
training.atoms_one_neighbour: An atom's number is how many bonds it takes. When it has only one neighbour it can still bond with, every bond it still needs goes there. Tap between two atoms for a bond, again for a double.
training.atoms_all_forced: A line holds two bonds at most, and a neighbour takes no more than it still needs. When an atom needs exactly as many bonds as its neighbours have room for, it uses all of them.
training.atoms_at_least_one: When an atom can leave only a little room unused, a neighbour with more room than that must take the difference. A 3 with two neighbours gets at least one bond each way.
training.atoms_crossing: Bonds can't cross. Once a bond is drawn, the line across it is shut, and that can leave an atom few enough ways for one of the rules before.
training.atoms_isolation: Every atom joins one molecule. A bond that would finish two atoms and cut them off from the rest (a 1 to a 1, a double between two 2s) can't be, and that can force a bond elsewhere.
training.atoms_what_if: Suppose a line had no bond and follow what that forces, a step or two. If an atom then can't reach its number, or a group is cut off, the line must have a bond.
training.chess_mate_in_one: One move ends it. Look at the king's squares: a check it can't escape by moving, by capturing the checker or by blocking is mate.
training.chess_forcing_key: With moves to spare, look at checks first: a check leaves the defence few replies. Find the one after which every reply still allows mate.
training.chess_quiet_key: Sometimes no check works and the key is a quiet move: it takes the king's last squares or sets up a threat the defence can't meet. Every reply must still allow mate.
training.cipher_leading: When the total is one letter longer than the numbers added, its first letter is the carry out of the last column. Two digits and a carry make at most 19, so that letter is 1.
training.cipher_column: Each column adds up on its own: its digits and the carry from the right end in the total's letter. When enough of a column is known, one letter has a single digit left.
training.cipher_pair: Take two neighbouring columns together, through the carry between them: each cuts what the other allows. Find the one digit that lets both add up.
training.cipher_chain: When no column or pair settles it, work every column and carry through together, giving no two letters the same digit, until a letter has one digit left.
training.cipher_what_if: Try every choice for two neighbouring columns at once, keeping what the other columns rule out. When only one digit for a letter lets both add up, that's its digit.
training.domino_only_partner: A free square with one free neighbour must share a domino with it. When only one domino in the tray can cover the two and keep the regions' rules, lay it there.
training.domino_only_place: Pick a domino in the tray and look at everywhere it could lie. When the regions' rules rule out all but one place, it goes there.
training.domino_only_domino: Pick a free square and ask which dominoes could cover it. When the rules of the regions around it rule out all but one, lay that one.
training.domino_region_value: A region's empty squares can only show values the tray can still put there. When those can't keep its rule with a domino lying somewhere, it can't lie there. See what that leaves.
training.domino_counting: Count a value's halves left in the tray. When exactly that many squares can take nothing else, no other square gets one, and that settles a domino.
training.domino_what_if: Try each domino that could cover a square and follow it a few steps. When all but one break a rule, the one left goes there.
training.kings_last_square: When a row, column or colour has one open square left, its king goes there. Crown it with a double-tap or a long press.
training.kings_locked: When a colour's open squares all lie in one row or column, its king is in that line, so the line's other squares can't hold one: cross them out. It works the other way round too, a line whose open squares all lie in one colour.
training.kings_would_empty: A king rules out its row, its column, its colour and the squares around it. When a king on a square would rule out every open square of some row, column or colour, it can't go there: cross it out.
training.kings_confined: The same as a colour locked to a line, with more of them: when two colours fit only in the same two rows (or columns), those lines' kings belong to them, so cross out the lines' other squares. Three in three works the same way.
training.kings_what_if: Suppose a king on a square and follow the last squares it forces. If that leaves a row, column or colour with no room at all, the square can't hold a king: cross it out.
training.lamps_zero: A 0 has no lamps beside it, so none of the squares next to it can hold one: tap them to cross them out.
training.lamps_done: When a number already has all its lamps beside it, the other squares next to it hold none: cross them out.
training.lamps_room: When a number still needs as many lamps as it has squares beside it that could take one (not walls, lamps, lit or crossed), they are all lamps. Double-tap or long-press for a lamp.
training.lamps_only_light: Every white square must be lit. When only one square left can light a dark square, whether itself or one in its row or column, that square holds a lamp.
training.lamps_starve: A lamp lights its whole row and column. When a lamp on a square would light so many squares beside a number that the number couldn't get its lamps, no lamp goes there: cross it out.
training.lamps_dark: When a lamp on a square would light every square that could light some dark square, without lighting that square itself, nothing could ever light it. So no lamp goes there: cross it out.
training.lamps_what_if: Suppose a lamp on a square, or none, and follow the numbers and squares it forces. If a number gets too many lamps or too few, or a square could never be lit, the other choice is the answer.
training.lits_whole_region: Every region holds one L, I, T or S of four squares. A region of exactly four squares is its own tetromino: shade all of it.
training.lits_overlap: Picture every L, I, T and S that fits in a region, around anything shaded there already. Squares every one of them covers are shaded whichever it is.
training.lits_avoid_block: No 2x2 block may be all shaded. Set aside a region's shapes that would finish one with the shading beside them, and shade what every shape left covers.
training.lits_letter_clash: Two tetrominoes of one letter may not touch edge to edge. Set aside a region's shapes that would touch a finished one of their own letter, and shade what every shape left covers.
training.lits_neighbour: Set aside a region's shapes that would leave a region beside it no shape at all, and shade what every shape left covers.
training.lits_what_if: Suppose a square stays empty and follow the shapes that forces. If some region is left with no shape at all, the square must be shaded.
training.mambo_pair: Two suns side by side can't have a third beside them, so the squares at either end are moons; the same goes the other way round. Tap a square once for a moon, twice for a sun.
training.mambo_sandwich: A gap between two matching symbols takes the other one: the same there would make three together.
training.mambo_link: An = says two squares match, an x says they differ. When one end is filled, the other follows.
training.mambo_quota: Every row and column holds as many suns as moons. When a line already has its half of one symbol, every square left in it is the other.
training.mambo_almost: A line one short of its half of one symbol: try its last one on each open square, the rest the other. Where that leaves three of the other together, the square can't take it.
training.mambo_what_if: Suppose a symbol on a square and follow the simple rules a round. If that breaks a rule somewhere, the square takes the other symbol.
training.mines_all_found: When a number already touches as many mines as it shows, every other hidden square around it is safe: reveal them. A 0 touches none, so everything around it is safe.
training.mines_all_mines: When a number has exactly as many hidden squares around it as mines it still needs, every one of them is a mine: flag them with a long press, or with Flag below.
training.mines_subset: Compare two numbers side by side. When every square where one still needs mines also touches the other, the other's extra squares hold the difference: none means they're safe, as many as there are squares means they're mines.
training.mines_pair: Two numbers that share squares: the shared squares can hold no more than the first still needs, so the second's squares outside them must hold the rest. When that's all of them, they're mines, and the first's own other squares are safe.
training.mines_edge: Count the mines left, shown above the board. When some numbers need every one of them on squares none of them share, no mine is left for any other hidden square: those are all safe.
training.mines_what_if: Suppose a square held a mine, or were safe, and follow what the numbers around it then say. If a number ends up with too many mines or too few squares, the other choice is the answer.
training.mosaic_count: Count the colours on the board against the fills left. A fill wipes out a colour only by covering its last patch, so with one fill fewer than colours, every fill must: pour into a colour that's down to one patch.
training.mosaic_biggest: Look for the fill that swallows the most neighbouring areas at once: an area touching several patches of one colour, poured that colour. It isn't always safe, but here it is.
training.mosaic_centre: When no fill swallows much, grow from the middle: find the area with every other area fewest steps away, and pour into it the colour that joins the most neighbours and stays in the limit.
training.nonogram_full: When a line's clues and the gaps between them take its whole width, there is nowhere to slide: fill every run and cross the gaps. Here the crosses count: use the Cross pen.
training.nonogram_finished: When a line already shows every run its clue asks for, none of its other squares can be filled: cross them out.
training.nonogram_overlap: Push a line's clues as far one way as they go, then as far the other. Squares a run covers both times are filled, wherever it ends up.
training.nonogram_line: With some squares of a line already marked, every way its clues can still fit may agree on a square. Fill it or cross it, whichever they all say. Here the crosses count: use the Cross pen.
training.pearls_black_pearl: The loop turns on a black pearl and runs straight on through the next square both ways. An arm it can't draw sends it the other way. Drag to draw a line; tap an edge to cross it.
training.pearls_white_pearl: The loop goes straight through a white pearl. When it can't go one way, for an edge crossed or the border, it runs straight through the other way.
training.pearls_white_turn: The loop turns just before or just after a white pearl. When it runs straight on through the square on one side, it must turn at the square on the other: cross the edge straight on from there.
training.pearls_one_way: A line can't stop. When the square at its end has only one way on left, the line goes there.
training.pearls_dead_end: A loop through a square needs two ways in. A square with only one way left can't be passed: cross its last edge.
training.pearls_small_loop: There is only one loop. Joining two ends of one line would close a loop that leaves out a pearl or another line, so cross the edge between them.
training.pearls_what_if: Suppose a line on an edge, or none, and follow the rules a few steps. If a square would need three lines or a pearl couldn't keep its rule, the edge goes the other way.
training.pipes_border: No pipe can point off the board. Against the edge a tile often fits one way only: a straight runs along it, a T turns its flat side to it, a bend in a corner has one way. Tap the tile to turn it.
training.pipes_set_neighbour: An opening must meet an opening. A set neighbour settles the side the two tiles share: open if it points in, shut if it doesn't. When the sides that settles leave one way round, turn the tile to it.
training.pipes_whichever_way: A neighbour that isn't set yet can still settle a side: when every way it could turn points into this tile, or none does, the shared side is settled whichever way it ends up.
training.pipes_no_loop: The pipes make no loops. When two tiles are already joined the long way round, they can't also join directly, so the side between them is shut. That can leave a tile only one way round.
training.shikaku_only_fits: A number is its rectangle's area. When the edges, the other numbers and the rectangles already drawn leave it just one way to lay that many squares out, draw it: drag from corner to corner.
training.shikaku_only_reaches: Every square belongs to some rectangle. When only one number's rectangles can reach an empty square, and just one of them covers it, that rectangle is the one.
training.shikaku_common_cells: When every rectangle a number can make covers the same squares, no other number can use them. Set them aside and see which number that leaves just one rectangle.
training.shikaku_what_if: Suppose a number took one of its other rectangles. If that leaves another number no room, or a square no number can reach, it can't go that way. Draw the one way left.
training.tally_done: When the circled numbers in a row or column already make its target, nothing else there can stay: remove the rest.
training.tally_too_big: Take what a line's circled numbers make from its target: that is all it still needs. A number bigger than that can't stay. Remove it.
training.tally_too_much: Add up what is left in a line and see how far over its target it is. A number bigger than that surplus can't go, or the line would fall short: circle it with Keep.
training.tally_all_left: When what is left in a line adds up to exactly its target, every number there stays: circle them all.
training.tally_ways: List the ways a line can still make its target. A number every way uses stays; one no way uses goes.
training.tally_what_if: Suppose a number stays (or goes) and follow the lines it settles. If some line is left with no way to make its target, the number does the opposite.
training.tents_no_tree: A tent sits right beside its tree: up, down, left or right. A square with no tree there can't hold one, so it's grass: tap it, or drag across several.
training.tents_line_done: When a row or column already has all the tents its number says, the rest of it is grass.
training.tents_line_full: When a row or column still needs as many tents as it has squares left that could hold one, they are all tents. Double-tap or long-press for a tent.
training.tents_one_spot: Every tree needs a tent beside it. When every other square next to a tree is a tree, off the board or grass, its tent goes on the one square left.
training.tents_shared: Tents never touch, not even at a corner. When a tent on a square would touch every spot left for some tree's tent, that square is grass.
training.tents_served: Each tent belongs to one tree. When every tree beside a square already has its own tent, a tent there would have no tree: it's grass.
training.whoswho_clue: Some clues settle a square on their own: "Ann has the cat" is a tick, "Ben isn't the pilot" a cross. Make the mark the clue gives.
training.whoswho_only: When everything else in a column is crossed off for someone, the one item left is theirs: tick it. It works down the table too: when everyone but one person is ruled out for an item, it's theirs.
training.whoswho_link: A clue that ties two things together carries what you know across. If the baker drinks tea and Ann is the baker, Ann drinks tea; if tea is ruled out for Ben, he isn't the baker either.
training.whoswho_house: Houses are numbered from the left. "Next to" and "left of" clues limit where someone can live: whoever lives left of someone can't be in the last house. Cross off the houses the clue rules out.
training.whoswho_what_if: Suppose a tick and follow the clues a few steps. If someone is left with nothing, or a clue can't hold, the tick was wrong: cross it off.
training.nonogram_keep_going: Keep going: crosses count here, so cross the squares the step rules out.
training.mosaic_aside: That fill works, it keeps you in the limit. This practice is after a different technique, so try it on another board.
